findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:1216-1221 (writeCodexProcessEvent) excludes ONLY entry.command==="quorum_submit" from the generic post-handler codex_cli process-event append, with a comment stating this is because quorum_submit "owns one exact immutable process-events transaction inside its handler" and a generic append "would make that canonical commit dirty again". quorum_prune (packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:20-22,338-365) commits process-events.jsonl through the IDENTICAL captureLifecycleMetadataTransaction/commitLifecycleMetadataTransaction machinery and its own header comment explicitly claims parity ("committed through the SAME lifecycle-metadata transaction machinery quorum_submit uses so the pre-dirty refusal, exact-content verification, and rollback all hold") — a claim also repeated in command-policy.ts:480 and process-fact-levels.ts:209, both touched by this diff. cli-engine.ts was NOT updated to add the matching exclusion for quorum_prune. Live repro (built dist, temp git fixture, LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex): `lattice quorum_prune --apply` succeeds and commits cleanly (HEAD advances, applied:true), but immediately after, `git status --porcelain` shows `M .lattice/story/actives/<id>/process-events.jsonl` — the exact file quorum_prune just atomically committed is re-dirtied by the unguarded generic codex_cli append, which is the precise poisoning mode the sibling comment for quorum_submit exists to prevent. This leftover dirty state then makes quorum_prune/quorum_submit pre-dirty-refuse on the very next call for reasons unrelated to genuine story changes. No test in packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts exercises `quorum_prune --apply` through the real CLI (runFixtureCli, which sets LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex) with a post-command git-status-clean assertion (unlike the existing quorum_submit CLI test at line ~939 which does assert `git status --porcelain=v1===`), so this gap is untested. WHY: the diff repeatedly promises quorum_prune has transactional parity with quorum_submit including pre-dirty-refusal integrity, but the one cross-file wiring point that actually protects that guarantee under Codex-driven sessions was left half-registered.
findings.resolvedReason: cli-engine.ts now excludes quorum_prune from the generic codex_cli process-event append, kept as its own literal statement because verify-process-fact-contract.mjs pins the quorum_submit line. New smoke check runs quorum_prune --apply through the built CLI under LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex and asserts git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all is empty. RED-verified: patching the exclusion out of the built dist made the check fail with exactly 'M .lattice/story/actives/B-quorum-smoke/process-events.jsonl'. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: handlers/quorum-prune.ts:125-135 writeUniqueBackup() writes the pre-prune backup directly into the git-tracked story dir (.lattice/story/actives/<id>/process-events.jsonl.bak-<ts>) and NEVER stages/commits/gitignores it (no matching *.bak-* gitignore pattern; the *.bak pattern at .gitignore does not match the .bak-<timestamp> suffix). Verified live: after `quorum_prune {apply:true}` succeeds, `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` in the story dir shows `?? .../process-events.jsonl.bak-<ts>` (repro output captured). Both assertCleanPruneBaseline (quorum-prune.ts:112-123, called at :336) and assertCleanQuorumBaseline (quorum-submit.ts:219-228, called at :529) do a raw whole-tree `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` with zero exemption for this file, so the very first legitimate follow-up action after a successful recovery -- another quorum_prune apply, OR a genuinely-new quorum_submit once the story-owned files change -- throws "worktree/index must be clean"/"nothing to prune" refusals caused entirely by the tool's own leftover backup, not by real user dirt. The same unexempted --untracked-files=all pattern is reused broadly (validation-executor.ts:202, done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts:362, dirty-worktree-gate.ts:42, recover-evidence.ts:68, cross-host-review.ts:81), so a leftover backup can also block TEST/DONE-adjacent gates. This directly undermines the story's stated goal ("the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level" / official low-friction recovery) since the operator must now manually discover and clean up (commit, delete, or gitignore) the tool's own artifact before doing anything else in the story. None of the 12 quorum_prune smoke checks catch this: the one test that runs quorum_prune apply twice ("never overwrites a previous run backup") masks it by doing its own `git add -A; git commit` between the two applies, which incidentally absorbs the first backup file into a commit -- a step a real operator/recovery workflow would not necessarily perform.
findings.resolvedReason: writeUniqueBackup now names the backup process-events.jsonl.<stamp>.bak with the collision counter BEFORE the extension, so every candidate genuinely matches the existing .gitignore *.bak rule. Neither assertCleanPruneBaseline nor assertCleanQuorumBaseline was weakened and no bespoke exemption was added. New smoke check runs apply twice in a row with NO intervening git command and the second apply succeeds. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-002:edge:2 evidence overclaims, packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:519-526 vs packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:1665-1669: intent requires the refusal message to be verified as naming standing runIds, materialDigest of the standing verdicts, and pointing at review_escalation_status. The production message does contain all of that, but the ONLY assertion against it anywhere in the smoke suite is assert.match(..., /quorum_submit refuses: .*drift-accept/i, ...) at line 1667 (and /drift-accept/i at 1711/1714) -- neither checks for runIds, materialDigest values, or the literal string review_escalation_status. The verificationEvidence note for CHK-002:edge:2 ("Drift-branch message content asserted via regex; message names standing runIds, older material(s), current storyFilesHash, poisoning consequence, and points at review_escalation_status") overstates what the bound regex actually verifies -- it is true of the production code, not of the test assertion.
findings.resolvedReason: The drift-accept refusal check now asserts the message contains all three standing runIds, the older materialDigest, the current storyFilesHash, and the literal review_escalation_status pointer, instead of only matching /drift-accept/. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-003:happy:2 evidence cites an unbound command, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2098-2113: the checklist scope.allowedModify explicitly includes packages/main/src/core/config.ts (DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS wiring), and config.ts:362 does add quorum_prune to DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS. But the bound checks own comment (~2106-2109) says exercising that wiring is "outside this storys scope contract" and is not tested there (only catalog+policy resolution and non-unknown-command dispatch are asserted). The verificationEvidence note for CHK-003:happy:2 instead claims coverage via "scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs passes with the new fact row and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS entry" -- but that script is a different, separate command from the one this evidence row is bound to (node packages/main/dist/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.js), and no verificationEvidence row records that script having been run at this headHash/materialHash. The claimed "wiring verification across all 5 integration points" is therefore not actually demonstrated by evidence bound to this storys own smoke command for the config.ts integration point.
findings.resolvedReason: The CLI-registration check now asserts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS['*'] contains quorum_prune and isCommandAllowed('quorum_prune','REVIEW') is true, with a negative control (plan_set refused in REVIEW) so the exit-0 is not vacuous. The stale out-of-scope disclaimer comment was removed; config.ts is in the story scope contract. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-002:adversarial:2 evidence overclaims, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:1622-1673: intent explicitly requires asserting hostVerdictEventCount, verdictFileCount, AND `git rev-parse HEAD` all unchanged after the drift-accept refusal (does not advance HEAD). The bound check (refuses a redundant re-submit when the standing quorum drift-accepts) captures beforeEvents/beforeVerdicts (lines 1640-1641) and asserts them unchanged (lines 1670-1671), but never captures or re-checks `git rev-parse HEAD` before/after the refusal -- unlike every other refusal-leaks-no-state check in this same file (e.g. lines 1545/1552, 1740/1745, 1877/1890, 1943/1951) which do assert HEAD is unchanged via beforeHead. One of the three required invariants in this adversarial intent is unverified.
findings.resolvedReason: The drift-accept refusal check now captures git rev-parse HEAD before the refusal and asserts it unchanged afterwards, matching the sibling refusal-leaks-no-state checks. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 evidence reuses happy:1 assertion, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:1622-1673 (lines 1633-1636): the intent explicitly states storyFilesHash equality is necessary but not sufficient and requires an independent check that commitMainDrift touches zero story-owned file blobs. The bound evidence reuses the exact same storyHashBefore===storyHashAfter assertion already used for CHK-001:happy:1 -- no distinct file-level/diff-based assertion exists anywhere in the suite verifying commitMainDrift only ever touches main-drift.ts; this is proven only by the note ("commitMainDrift helper commits only ... - no story-diff file is touched"), which is a claim about the helpers hardcoded implementation, not an independent runtime check as the intent explicitly demanded.
findings.resolvedReason: New storyOwnedDiffBlobs() helper reads git diff --raw (path, status, destination blob id) between merge-base(main,HEAD) and HEAD filtered by isMaterialExcludedPath. CHK-001:edge:0 now asserts that set is non-empty, deepEqual across the drift, and never contains main-drift.ts, while a whole-tree diff proves the drift really landed main-drift.ts. Shares no code with the storyFilesHash digest. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: CHK-003 (quorum_prune) test-coverage gap, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2245-2268: no check anywhere in the 12 quorum_prune checks asserts the worktree is clean immediately after a successful `quorum_prune {apply:true}`. quorum-prune.ts:161-169 lifecycleMetadataPaths(kind=quorum-submit) scopes the commit to ONLY process-events.jsonl; writeUniqueBackup() (quorum-prune.ts:125-135, called at :351) writes process-events.jsonl.bak-<timestamp> directly into the tracked story dir and it is never staged/committed by that scoped transaction. .gitignore:32 `*.bak` does not match the `.bak-<timestamp>` suffix, so the backup is left untracked. assertCleanPruneBaseline/assertCleanQuorumBaseline both run an unscoped `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all`, so the very next quorum_prune or quorum_submit call would refuse on the tools own leftover artifact -- verified live by re-running quorum_prune {apply:true} in a fresh fixture right after a first apply with no intervening commit: it refuses nothing-to-prune only after the backup is manually cleaned. The ONE check that runs prune twice (quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2245 never overwrites a previous run backup) masks this because it does its own git add -A + commit between the two applies (lines ~2261-2262), which is not a step a real recovery operator performs. So CHK-003 happy path claim (userSees: the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level / official low-friction recovery) is unverified at the worktree-cleanliness level and is contradicted once you try the very next legitimate action. (Independently corroborates a live concurrent lattice-review-quality RR-003 finding on the same defect, verified here from the test-coverage angle: no verificationEvidence row demonstrates clean-after-apply.)
findings.resolvedReason: Same root cause as F-002 and fixed by the same change: the backup now matches the *.bak ignore rule so a real operator's second recovery call works with no manual git commands. The new twice-apply smoke check has no intervening git add/commit, so it can no longer mask the leftover-artifact failure. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: CHK-003 userSees literally documents `lattice quorum_prune --storyId=... --dryRun lists the duplicate verdict events...; without --dryRun it backs up, removes them, commits...`, and plan.md CHK-003 specifies the command input as `dryRun` (default true) requiring explicit `apply:true` to mutate. But packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2994-3001 (quorum_prune schema) and packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:34-39 (QuorumPruneArgs) define ONLY an `apply` field — there is no `dryRun` field anywhere in the schema or handler. Empirically verified live against the real repo: `node bin/lattice.js quorum_prune --storyId=B-3144` (no flags at all, i.e. omitting --dryRun exactly as userSees describes) still prints `mode: dry-run (no mutation)` — it does NOT back up/remove/commit as userSees claims. The `--dryRun` flag is silently swallowed as an unrecognized key (flag-parser.ts has no schema-strictness) and has zero effect on behavior; the only way to actually mutate is the undocumented-in-userSees `--apply` flag. An operator following the story's own documented usage would be misled about how to trigger the recovery.
findings.resolvedReason: quorum_prune now declares a real dryRun boolean in both the catalog schema and QuorumPruneArgs, following the capability_release_backfill convention (default true unless apply=true). --dryRun is honored instead of being silently swallowed, and dryRun:true combined with apply:true is refused before any file read or mutation. Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered (same root cause as F-008): because quorum_prune has no `dryRun` schema field, packages/main/src/cli/help-renderer.ts:150-151 dryRunHelpLine() falls through its no-dryRun-field branch, matches /dry-run/i against the tool description text, and prints `Dry-run: always-on. This command only projects guidance and does not execute the side-effect path.` in `node bin/lattice.js quorum_prune --help` — empirically verified live. This is actively wrong: `apply:true` performs a real mutating side effect (writes a timestamped backup, rewrites the committed process-events.jsonl, and creates a git commit via captureLifecycleMetadataTransaction/commitLifecycleMetadataTransaction in packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:338-366). For a recovery command whose entire safety design (plan.md Risks section) rests on dry-run-by-default + explicit apply, the auto-generated --help text tells operators the opposite of the truth about when it mutates state.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by the same dryRun schema field: help-renderer now derives the default-on branch, so --help prints 'Dry-run: default-on via --dryRun=true ... Default true unless apply=true; passing dryRun:true together with apply:true is refused' instead of the inverted 'Dry-run: always-on. This command only projects guidance and does not execute the side-effect path.' Commit f1bcba3885.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: CHK-003 userSees (.lattice/story/actives/B-3144/checklist.json) still literally claims `lattice quorum_prune --storyId=... --dryRun lists...; without --dryRun it backs up, removes them, commits, and the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level.` Empirically re-verified live against the CURRENT committed code (post f1bcba3885, dist rebuilt): `node bin/lattice.js quorum_prune --storyId=B-3144` (no --dryRun flag at all, exactly the without-dryRun case userSees describes) and `quorum_prune {"storyId":"B-3144","dryRun":false}` BOTH still print `mode: dry-run (no mutation)` and do NOT back up/remove/commit. In packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:214-221, the mutating apply path is gated SOLELY by explicit `apply:true` (`const apply = args.apply === true;` ... `if (!apply) { ...dryRun:true... }`); the newly-added `dryRun` field (F-008 fix) only participates in the apply+dryRun conflict-refusal check, it never itself flips execution into the apply branch. F-008/F-009 fixed the swallowed-flag and inverted --help wording, but did not correct this specific userSees clause, which still conflates omitting --dryRun with passing --apply=true. Live CLI output (`note: dry-run only — re-run with apply:true...`) does self-correct an attentive operator, so this is not a safety inversion like the original F-009, but the story checklist itself still documents a behavior the current code does not deliver.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 7eb91080fd by making the behavior match the frozen userSees rather than editing the promise. An explicit dryRun:false now executes exactly like apply:true (quorum-prune.ts: apply = args.apply === true || args.dryRun === false), so the flag is no longer a silent no-op. Omitting dryRun still defaults to the safe projection, and apply:true + dryRun:true is still refused, so neither the safety default nor the repo convention (capability_release_backfill) was weakened. New smoke check quorum_prune dryRun:false executes instead of being a silent no-op asserts both directions: omitted = no commit and no backup; explicit false = commit + backup + 6 removed verdicts + clean tree. Smoke 61 to 62 green, process-fact contract verified, npm test exit 0.

findings.desc: doc-behavior-mismatch: F-010 (commit 7eb91080fd) made dryRun:false an executor equal to apply:true, and updated ONLY command-catalog.ts:2997 (the dryRun field describe()) and the function-local comment at quorum-prune.ts:208-218 to say so. Five other prose locations describing the exact same apply/dryRun semantics were left stale, still claiming apply:true is required/the only way to mutate: (1) quorum-prune.ts:20 module comment "dry-run is the default (no mutation without explicit apply:true...)"; (2) quorum-prune.ts:198 user-facing dry-run note "re-run with apply:true to back up, prune, and commit" (never mentions dryRun:false); (3) command-catalog.ts:2994 the TOP-LEVEL tool description shown first in `lattice quorum_prune --help` output — "list (dry-run by default) and, with apply:true, remove duplicate host_verdict events" — inconsistent with the correctly-updated --dryRun flag description three lines below it in the SAME --help output; (4) process-fact-levels.ts:209 rationale "apply:true required to mutate"; (5) command-policy.ts:480 reason "apply:true required to mutate". Verified live: `node bin/lattice.js quorum_prune --help` prints the stale top-level description at line 1 and the corrected --dryRun description a few lines later, an internal inconsistency visible in the same output block. Before F-010 these five statements were true; the F-010 commit made them false without updating them. No test asserts command-catalog.ts:2994, process-fact-levels.ts:209, or command-policy.ts:480 text, so nothing catches this. Not a broken user promise (apply:true still works) but a genuine half-updated-documentation defect: an operator or auditor reading only the top-level description or the policy/process-fact rationale forms an incorrect mental model of the mutation trigger.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit e306cc7aad. All five stale prose sites now name both executors: quorum-prune.ts module comment (rewritten to state dry-run is the default and execution requires apply:true or the equivalent dryRun:false, with both contradictory pairs refused), quorum-prune.ts dry-run note text, command-catalog.ts top-level description (the first --help line, which had contradicted the corrected flag description in the same output), process-fact-levels.ts rationale, and command-policy.ts reason. A new smoke check 'every quorum_prune apply/dryRun description states both executors' reads the three source files directly and asserts each description mentions dryRun:false and no longer claims apply:true is the only mutation trigger, so this drift cannot silently recur.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:219-226 (F-010 fix): the conflict refusal only catches apply:true && dryRun:true. It does not catch the symmetric conflict apply:false && dryRun:false — verified live: with args={apply:false,dryRun:false}, `const apply = args.apply === true || args.dryRun === false` evaluates to true, so the command silently EXECUTES (backs up, rewrites, commits) even though the caller explicitly passed apply:false. This breaks the code's own stated design philosophy (comment at line ~211-218 and the existing apply:true+dryRun:true refusal): an explicitly conflicting combination should be REFUSED, not silently resolved toward the more dangerous (mutating) outcome. Reachable via both programmatic args and CLI (--apply=false --dryRun=false parses to {apply:false,dryRun:false} per cli/flag-parser.ts coerce()). Fix: extend the refusal check to `(args.apply === true && args.dryRun === true) || (args.apply === false && args.dryRun === false)`, or otherwise treat an explicit apply:false as an unconditional veto regardless of dryRun.
